key_terms.إِرَمَ: A tribe or city known for its grandeur
key_terms.ذَاتِ الْعِمَادِ: Possessor of the pillars, referring to tall architectural structures

ai.seo_question: Who were the people of Iram and what does 'Dhat al-Imad' mean?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, 'Iram of the Pillars' is often interpreted not merely as a physical tribe but as a symbol of arrogant power and architectural hubris that defied divine authority, paralleling the fate of Pharaoh. This phrase serves as a potent reminder of God's ability to dismantle even the most fortified civilizations, reinforcing the theme of divine retribution against the disbelievers in Surah Al-Fajr. The mention underscores the transient nature of worldly grandeur when disconnected from spiritual humility.
